newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hapoalim in finance pact with China banks.
newsitem.headline: Hapoalim in finance pact with China banks.

text.p: Israel's Bank Hapoalim said on Wednesday it had signed framework agreements with two Chinese banks to finance long-term trade deals.

Hapoalim said the deals signed last week with the Bank of China and the Shanghai-based Bank of Communications made it the first Israeli bank to reach such framework agreements that met the criteria of a 1996 Israel-China financial protocol.

"These framework agreements will allow deals to go through without the need for additional negotiations with Chinese banks, which is generally a long and complex process," Hapoalim, Israel's largest bank, said in a statement.
The bank said there were currently several deals on the agenda worth tens of millions of dollars with leading Israeli exporters.
Hapoalim added that negotiations with other Chinese banks were at an advanced stage and that it expected to sign further trade finance deals in coming weeks.

The 1996 financial protocol set out conditions under which Chinese importers could purchase Israeli equipment. The protocol called for Israeli banks to open credit lines to Chinese banks to finance purchases.
Hapoalim said that until now no Israeli bank succeeded in reaching financing agreements to allow transactions under the protocol.
